answer: To deter Sybil attacks, the network applies topological cut verifications across interaction graphs, where an honest peer cluster acts as an anchor and a high-throughput settlement hub serves as an execution wharf. When multi-agent auditing uncovers synthetic cycles or isolated subgraphs, consensus penalizes the colluding group through stake slashing, turning an attacker's bonded capital into a worthless relic while scaling Sybil expansion costs exponentially.
